# AGENTS.md - nvsnap documentation

Rules for anyone, person or agent, who adds to or changes nvsnap's
documentation under this directory. `make check-docs` (and the `nvsnap docs`
workflow) enforces the ones a script can check; the rest are for review.

## Where a document goes

| Kind | Where |
|---|---|
| Entry points | [START-HERE.md](START-HERE.md), then [README.md](README.md) (the index), then [GLOSSARY.md](GLOSSARY.md) |
| How nvsnap works | [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md): the one technical document. A behaviour change updates its section in the same PR |
| Every number | [RESULTS.md](RESULTS.md), with the record it comes from under `results/` |
| Working notes behind an architecture section | `design/`, each opening with a status line |
| Recipes: install, operate, develop | `operate/` |
| A dated run: a benchmark, a test campaign | `results/`; a record, not maintained |
| A superseded document | Nowhere: delete it (git history keeps it), after moving any still-true rule into ARCHITECTURE.md and any result that has no other record into RESULTS.md |

The top level holds only START-HERE, ARCHITECTURE, RESULTS, GLOSSARY,
REFERENCE, README and this file. A new document goes into
[README.md](README.md) in the same commit that adds it, with what it answers
and its status.

## What every document does

- Uses the [glossary](GLOSSARY.md)'s words with their meanings, and none of
  its retired words. A new term goes into the glossary in the same commit.
- Names the code behind a claim by path and symbol
  (`internal/agent/criu_group.go` `captureOptedIn`), not by line number.
- States a rule as the condition and the code that enforces it; states a
  limit as what is not done.
- Describes a cluster by its hardware ("4x GB300, driver 610"; "H100, EKS with
  NVMesh storage"), never by its name, and names no internal host, address or
  personal path.
- Cites no file that is not in this repository, such as a personal agent
  instructions file.
- When it finds another document that disagrees with the code, adds a row to
  [ARCHITECTURE.md §14](ARCHITECTURE.md#14-where-other-documents-disagree-with-the-code)
  or fixes that document in the same PR.

## Numbers

Every number names the hardware, the date and the nvsnap build ("not
recorded" when the record does not say), and links the record it comes from.
A number with no record is left out. A number found wrong is withdrawn in
[RESULTS.md](RESULTS.md), in place, with the reason; it is not silently
replaced.

## Figures

Review-grade figures follow the NVIDIA Cloud Architecture Diagrams style,
through the `nvaf-architecture-diagrams` skill in
`.agents/skills/` (copied unchanged from the nvaf repository, as flashbox and
bedrock do). Each figure is an SVG drawn by its own script under
`figures/scripts/`, with a light and a dark PNG rendered beside it by
`figures/scripts/render.sh`; a document embeds the SVG with
`![alt](figures/<name>.svg)`. Look at both PNGs before committing, and commit
the script, the SVG and the PNGs together. Mermaid is for quick inline
sketches. How to regenerate: [figures/README.md](figures/README.md).

## Generated pages

- [REFERENCE.md](REFERENCE.md) is generated from the Go sources by
  `scripts/docs/reference.py`; rerun it after changing an annotation, an
  environment variable or an agent route.
- Tables of contents are generated by `scripts/docs/docs-toc.py` between
  their marker comments; edit the headings, never the list.

## Before you push

```bash
make -C src/compute-plane-services/nvsnap check-docs
```

It fails on a broken link, heading anchor or doc path (in documents, code,
scripts and the chart), a stale table of contents, a REFERENCE.md that no
longer matches the code, and a figure that no longer matches its script.
The repository's `markdown-lint` workflow checks style.
